title: Data Processing Schedule & Security Attachment — SaaS Integrations (WORKING DRAFT)
content:
WORKING DRAFT - FOR INTERNAL REVIEW ONLY

Purpose and scope
This Data Processing Schedule and Security Attachment (the "Attachment") supplements the underlying Master Services Agreement ("MSA") or Data Processing Agreement between Redwood Inference ("Processor") and the Customer ("Controller"). It defines the specific processing activities, categories of personal data, security measures, and operational commitments that apply to SaaS integrations where Customer data is processed by Redwood-hosted services, dedicated instances, or Private deployments managed under the Redwood platform.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an internal working draft intended to consolidate security commitments and operational SLAs relevant to sales/solutions discussions for mid-market and enterprise customers.
- Open issues: breach notification SLA (24 vs 48 hours), encryption key management options for Private deployments, and logging retention defaults. See linked JIRA ticket SEC-1543 for discussion threads.

1) Definitions (key terms used in this Attachment)
Controller/Customer: organization contracting with Redwood that determines purposes and means of processing.
Processor/Redwood: Redwood Inference, the party processing personal data on behalf of Controller.
Personal Data: any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person processed in the course of providing the Services.
Subprocessor: any third party engaged by Redwood to process Personal Data.
Security Incident / Personal Data Breach: unauthorized access, disclosure, loss, or destruction of Personal Data.

2) Data processing details
- Subject matter: delivery and operation of Redwood inference services and related features (text generation, embeddings, routing, observability hooks) invoked by Customer.
- Duration: for the term of the applicable Services subscription plus any legally required retention periods; specific retention windows may be set per Project/Customer in Console.
- Purpose(s): to provide, maintain, operate, improve, and secure the Services; to provide customer support and troubleshooting; to detect abuse and fraud; and to comply with law enforcement requests as required by law.
- Types of personal data: identifiers (name, email, account ID), authentication data (hashed passwords, tokens), usage/telemetry (IP addresses, request/response metadata, timestamps), content data (Customer-provided prompts and generated content may include personal data), billing and contact details.
- Categories of data subjects: end users, account administrators, authorized integrators, and Customer personnel.

3) Processing constraints and Controller instructions
- Processor will process Personal Data only on documented instructions from Controller as set forth in the MSA, order forms, and this Attachment. For ambiguous processing requests, Redwood will request clarification and will not materially process outside documented scope.
- Controller may instruct deletion or export using the Console APIs. Redwood will provide tooling for bulk export of data formats commonly used in integrations (JSON/NDJSON).

4) Subprocessors
- Redwood maintains a list of Subprocessors used for hosting, monitoring, payments, and analytics. Redwood will provide a current Subprocessor list upon Customer request and will give notice of material additions.
- Controller may object to a new Subprocessor within 15 days; parties will use commercially reasonable efforts to address such concerns. If not resolvable, Controller may terminate affected Services for the impacted environment upon written notice.
- Typical categories: cloud infrastructure providers, managed logging/observability vendors, KMS/HSM providers, CDN providers, security scanning vendors.

5) Security measures (baseline – applies to Hosted and Dedicated; Private deployment options noted)
Administrative controls:
- Access controls: role-based access control (RBAC) across Console and internal tools; least-privilege principle for employee accounts; automated offboarding integrations with IdP.
- Personnel: background-checked employees; mandatory security and privacy training; documented access approval workflows.

Technical controls:
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+/strong cipher suites in transit; AES-256 or equivalent at rest for hosted datasets; option for customer-managed keys (CMKs) in Dedicated/Private (KMS integration notes below).
- Key management: Hosted by default uses Redwood-managed KMS; Dedicated/Private customers may request BYOK/CMK integration subject to operational agreement and additional fees.
- Authentication & session management: OAuth2/OpenID Connect support for Console; JWT token lifetimes configurable; refresh token rotation.
- Network segmentation: tenant isolation via virtual networks, strict firewall rules, and VPC peering options for Private deployments.
- Logging & monitoring: immutable request/response logs retained for a default 90 days for debugging/security; extended retention available as paid add-on. Logs redact high-risk data by default (see Data Redaction section).
- Data minimization & pseudonymization: for telemetry and analytics, identifiers replaced with hashed pseudonyms where practical; PII is minimized in aggregated metrics.

Operational controls:
- Vulnerability management: periodic internal and external scanning; patch windows and emergency patching SLA for critical vulnerabilities (72 hours for critical CVEs affecting customer data).
- Pen-testing: annual third-party penetration tests; executive summary and remediation plan shared under NDA upon request.
- Change management: scheduled maintenance windows published in Console and automated change notifications for impactful changes.

6) Data retention, deletion, and return
- Customer Controls: Controller can export, archive, or request deletion of tenant data via Console APIs. Redwood will provide one full export in machine-readable format at termination without additional fee.
- Deletion timeline: Upon confirmed termination or delete request, Redwood will remove production-accessible copies within 30 days and scrub backups within 90 days unless retention is required by applicable law.
- Verification: Customer may request a deletion certificate; Redwood will provide a standard certificate template and allow for agreed verification procedures under NDA.

7) Breach notification and incident response
- Notification timeline: Redwood will notify Controller of confirmed Personal Data Breaches affecting Customer Personal Data without undue delay and in any event within 48 hours of confirmation of breach facts. (Open item: consider 24-hour target for enterprise contracts.)
- Contents of notification: summary of incident, types of data affected, remediation actions, risk mitigation steps, and point of contact.
- For critical incidents, Redwood will provide near real-time status via designated incident channel and offer a root cause analysis within 30 days of incident closure.
- Controller obligations: Controller will cooperate in incident response and provide timely information as reasonably required by Redwood.

8) Cross-border transfers and lawful basis
- Redundant operations across regions: Redwood operates in multiple cloud regions. Processing that involves cross-border transfer will be governed by the MSA/DPA clauses. For transfers from the EEA, Redwood will rely on standard contractual clauses (SCCs) or other lawful transfer mechanisms as agreed in the MSA.

9) Audit, compliance, and certifications
- Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications for core Hosted services. For Dedicated/Private deployments, certification scope is defined per deployment and may require additional attestation.
- Audit rights: Controller may request reasonable audit rights (on-site or remote) once per 12-month period subject to confidentiality, scope limitations, and reimbursement of Redwood's external audit costs for audits beyond routine compliance.

10) Data subject rights and cooperation
- Redwood will assist Controller with commercially reasonable efforts to respond to data subject requests relating to Personal Data processed on behalf of Controller (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability) in accordance with Controller's instructions.

11) Liability and remedies (summary)
- Security obligations do not limit warranted service levels. Standard liability caps and carve-outs will be as set in the MSA; parties may negotiate higher caps for enterprise-tier contracts.

12) Operational options & add-ons (commercial/implementation notes)
- BYOK/CMK integration for Dedicated/Private (requires runbook and compliance assessment).
- Extended logging retention (12 months+) as paid add-on.
- Enhanced audit package (attestation, evidence collection) for customers with stringent compliance requirements.
- Optional on-prem connector for isolated ingestion, referred to in implementation design docs.

13) Data handling examples and redaction guidance (practical)
- Prompts & Responses: Customer is responsible for redaction of highly sensitive personal data in prompts transmitted to the Service. Redwood provides client-side SDK helpers and best-practice examples (see internal repo and Confluence link) for pattern-based redaction prior to ingestion.
- Console Exports: exported data sets will include metadata and content unless explicitly redacted by Controller.

14) Termination, survival, and transition
- The obligations related to confidentiality, security, deletion, and return of Personal Data survive termination for the period necessary to accomplish secure deletion and legal retention.

15) Approval and next steps
- Legal review required: Priya Reddy (Legal) - complete.
- Engineering review required: SRE & Platform sign-off on encryption options for Dedicated - in progress (see JIRA SEC-1543).
- Customer-facing version: create a customer-friendly one-page summary and an FAQ for common questions (responsibility, export process, breach SLA options).

References and linked artifacts:
- Internal Confluence: SEC-Data-Processing-Schedule-v1 (draft)
- JIRA: SEC-1543 (open issues list)
- GitHub: repo/legal/dps-attachment#12 (draft PR with redline)

Unresolved items (for triage):
- Decide breach notification target (24 vs 48 hours) for enterprise vs self-serve customers.
- Finalize default log retention and redact policy for prompt/response content.
- Approve deletion certificate format for high-compliance customers.

End of working draft.

Document history: initial draft by Sofia Chen 2024-11-20. Major updates: consolidated subprocessor language and added BYOK notes 2025-01-10 (Ethan Morales). Latest edits to breach notification and retention language 2025-03-01 (Maya Lopez).
